acceptanceCriteria: corvint-tasks dispatch and dispatch status resolve a relative --config against the working directory (then apply the existing safe-open rules), or refuse it with a message saying the path must be absolute under a code other than UNSUPPORTED_FILESYSTEM
the unclean-path rule is applied consistently: an absolute --config containing '..' or '.' segments is either cleaned and accepted or refused, matching the documented rule
tests cover cfg/x.json, ./cfg/x.json, ../d/cfg/x.json, /abs/x/../cfg/x.json and /abs/cfg/x.json; GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#900 is closed by the PR
body: Reported in GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#900 (2026-10-15, macOS, corvint-tasks 0.0.0-tcp01-unverified). corvint-tasks dispatch status --program P --config cfg/dispatch.json (also ./cfg/... and ../d/cfg/...) refuses UNSUPPORTED_FILESYSTEM 'cannot open: unclean absolute directory "cfg"', while /abs/x/../cfg/dispatch.json and /abs/cfg/dispatch.json pass. The message comes from internal/tasks/safeopen/open_unix.go:83 ("unclean absolute directory"), which receives the relative directory unresolved. Expected: relative paths resolve against cwd, or a clear 'must be absolute' refusal; '..' handling consistent. Actual: misleading code and wording, inverted rule. Confirmed by source location; reproduction is the issue's table.
title: corvint-tasks dispatch --config refuses every relative path as 'unclean absolute directory' (UNSUPPORTED_FILESYSTEM) but accepts absolute paths with '..' (#900)
